transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi doctor. I'm here because I've been having a really hard time staying focused on things, whether it's at work or just daily tasks. I just can't seem to keep my attention on one thing for very long, and it's becoming a big problem for me.
Have you had trouble paying attention since childhood, or did this start more recently? If it started recently, was there a major stress, depression, or anxiety around that time?

This actually isn't a recent thing; I've struggled with paying attention since I was a kid, definitely before the age of 12. It has been a constant, persistent issue for over two years now, rather than something triggered by recent stress or anxiety.

Besides trouble focusing, do you also often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, talk excessively, or act impulsively? These can help me tell whether this is mainly inattentive ADHD or the combined type.

No, I don't really experience restlessness, fidgeting, or acting impulsively at all. I have no trouble sitting still and don't feel like I talk excessively. My difficulties are pretty much limited to focusing on tasks and keeping myself organized.
Do you often make careless mistakes, lose things, forget appointments, or avoid tasks that need a lot of mental effort? How much are these problems affecting your work, home life, or relationships?

To be honest, I don't really experience making careless mistakes, losing things, forgetting appointments, or avoiding tasks. Because of that, I'm not really sure if those specific issues have had any major impact on my work or relationships.

When your focus gets worse, do you also have a lot of uncontrollable worry, or feel down, lose interest in things, or have changes in sleep or energy? If so, which came first—the mood/anxiety symptoms or the concentration problems?

No, I don't really have uncontrollable worry, feel down, or experience changes in my sleep or energy. My struggles are really just with my concentration and focus, which have always been the primary issues for me.
Do you often find your mind wandering during conversations or reading, have trouble following through on instructions, or get easily distracted by unrelated thoughts or things around you?

Yes, absolutely. My mind constantly wanders during conversations or when I'm trying to read, and I get easily distracted by random thoughts or whatever is happening around me. It makes it incredibly hard to sustain my attention on any task.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home, and were they also noticeable at school when you were younger?

Yes, definitely. I struggle with staying focused and organized both at work and at home during my daily routine. These issues were also very noticeable back in elementary school, as I always had a hard time keeping up with my schoolwork.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks once you start them, or keeping things in order even when you’re trying to stay organized?

Yes, absolutely. I frequently struggle to stay focused enough to actually finish tasks once I start them, often leaving things half-done. Keeping my daily tasks, schedule, and physical spaces organized also feels extremely difficult, even when I make a real effort to do so.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning before age 12, present across school, work, and home settings, and persisting for over two years. Confirmed symptoms include difficulty sustaining attention, mind wandering, distractibility, trouble finishing tasks, and disorganization. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are denied, and there is no evidence from the interview that anxiety or depressive disorders better explain the concentration problems.
